rounds.proof_sketch: After __syncthreads(), shared_sum[0] is identical for all 256 threads. Original: tid==0 writes V=shared_sum[0]/element_count. Mutant: tid!=0 (threads 1-255) all write the same V. CUDA guarantees multiple threads writing same 32-bit aligned value yields that value. Result identical for all inputs.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the write condition from 'only thread 0 writes' to 'threads 1-255 write', but does not change what value is written. After the parallel reduction and final __syncthreads(), all threads observe the identical shared_sum[0] value. In the mutant, threads 1-255 all compute and write the same correct result to output[batch_idx]. Per CUDA's memory model, concurrent writes of the same value to a naturally aligned address are deterministic. The final_mean_kernel then reads the correctly computed batch_means values, producing identical output to the original.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutant produces identical output for all possible inputs because all writing threads compute and store the exact same value
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for CUDA kernels should consider that relational operator mutations on thread-id conditionals may be semantically equivalent when multiple threads compute identical values. Better mutation targets would be arithmetic operations within the computation itself, not just the write-back conditions.
